disease_label_per_paper: Rare presentation of abdominal wall erysipelas involving the anterior abdominal wall and breast
presentation_summary: 52-year-old immunocompetent woman presented with one day of subjective fever, chills, abdominal wall erythema, and pain.

She had fatigue, anorexia, body aches, and initially mild erythema surrounding the umbilicus, followed by severe diffuse erythema involving the entire anterior abdominal wall and bilateral inframammary areas.
She had an umbilical piercing one year before presentation; the authors considered the belly button piercing the likely port of entry.
On admission, temperature was 99.1 F, blood pressure 125/84 mmHg, heart rate 72/min, and respiratory rate 16/min.
Exam showed diffuse erythema and tenderness of the anterior abdominal wall with no papules, vesicles, or pustules.
Labs showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, high CRP, normal lactate, negative HIV Ag/Ab, negative blood cultures after five days, and elevated anti-DNase B.
CT abdomen with IV contrast showed focal fat stranding in the anterior abdominal wall and left paraumbilical region.
The belly ring was removed, IV cefazolin was started, and erythema/pain improved over two days with CRP down-trending; two-week follow-up showed complete resolution.
